discovery: Quantum ground-state preparation and quantum control of macroscopic mechanical oscillators

nominees.name: Andrew N. Cleland
nominees.affiliation: University of Chicago, Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering

nominees.name: Markus Aspelmeyer
nominees.affiliation: University of Vienna and IQOQI Vienna, Austrian Academy of Sciences

motivation: These three nominees brought vibrating mechanical objects, made of billions of atoms and visible under a microscope, into the quantum regime. In 2010 Cleland and co-workers coupled a piezoelectric resonator to a superconducting qubit, cooled it to its quantum ground state and created and measured single phonons. Aspelmeyer and Kippenberg founded cavity optomechanics. They used radiation-pressure sideband cooling to reach the ground state with light, and they demonstrated strong coupling, squeezing and entanglement between light and mechanical motion. Like macroscopic quantum tunnelling in Josephson junctions, this work shows that quantum mechanics applies to engineered macroscopic degrees of freedom. The experiments are clean and decisive, and they required noise to be driven below the quantum limit. The resulting devices now serve as quantum transducers, as force and displacement sensors at the standard quantum limit, and as platforms for tests of gravity and decoherence at large mass.
